name: Philippine Sign Language
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog refs are syntax/survey works only (Domingo 2022, Bautista & Rojas 2022, Hurlbut 2008); no phonology treating stress/prominence found for this sign language.

sources.citation: Tabingo, Shiela D. & Ana Helena R. Lovitos. 2025. Analyzing Filipino Sign Language through Systemic Functional Linguistics. IJRISS IX(II): 4423-4434. DOI 10.47772/IJRISS.2025.9020347
sources.note: Nothing on stress/prominence; mentions non-manual signals (raised eyebrows, head tilt) marking questions and calls modality-specific phonology future work. Its reference list is the only place the earlier scan's 'Bautista & Rojas 2022' occurs ('The syntax of Filipino Sign Language... Journal of Sign Language Linguistics 23(1): 75-91'); Crossref matches neither this nor several other FSL items in that list — treat as unverifiable.

sources.citation: Wang, Jianwei. 2024. Iconicity in Chinese Sign Language and Filipino Sign Language. English Language Teaching 17(5): 51-59. DOI 10.5539/elt.v17n5p51
sources.note: Nothing on FSL phonology or stress; iconic devices only.

sources.citation: Hurlbut, Hope M. 2008. Philippine Signed Languages Survey: A Rapid Appraisal. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008-010. SIL International. 16 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or prominence. Lexicostatistical rapid appraisal (2004-05 wordlists in SignWriting); pp. 8-9 compare signs by Liddell & Johnson (1989) parameters — handshape, location, movement, orientation, contact, non-manuals — only as similarity criteria. Finds two sign languages in the country (FSL and Samar Sign Language). Bibliography (p. 15) gives the full citation and URL of Apurado & Agravante 2006, the only FSL phonology paper located. sil.org is Cloudflare-blocked from our machine; fetched sources from the Wayback capture of 2024-01-10.

sources.citation: Martinez, Liza B. & Ed Peter G. Cabalfin. 2008. Sign Language and Computing in a Developing Country: A Research Roadmap for the Next Two Decades in the Philippines. PACLIC 22, 438-444.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States (p. 438) that the earliest descriptive work on FSL structure is Liza Martinez's from the early 1990s and that 'the most comprehensive linguistics reference' is PDRC & PFD 2004, An Introduction to Filipino Sign Language; also cites PFD 2005/2007 regional sign compilations. Open at https://aclanthology.org/.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page phil1239; Wikipedia (en) 'Filipino Sign Language'; Wikipedia (tl) 'Wikang Senyas ng mga Pilipino'
sources.note: No phonology or stress content. Glottolog lists one descriptive reference (Domingo 2022) plus Wilson 2016 and Ethnologue 2025. Wikipedia references are news, legal texts, Abat & Martinez 2006 (history), Notarte-Balanquit 2021 (summit report).
